sourceQuantifiedLines.line: 2.65 Billion USD in 2025, Projected to Reach 25.26 Billion USD by 2032 with a CAGR of 38.0%.
In 2025, the worldwide AI companion app market reached USD 2.65 Billion .
The market then moved onto a steep growth path, with projections pointing to USD 25.26 Billion by 2032.
That implies a 38.0% CAGR across the forecast window.

In this market, the climb from USD 3.55 Billion in 2026 to USD 25.26 Billion in 2032 reflects sustained expansion rather than a one-off spike, suggesting that app makers keep adding capabilities while maintaining the pricing and delivery logic needed to scale.
North America led the AI companion app market in 2025, capturing nearly 40.1% of global spend.
In 2025, North America sat at the top of the worldwide AI companion app market with an estimated USD 1,063.25 Million and a 40.1% share of global revenue.
Asia Pacific followed with an estimated 31.1% share, representing USD 823.89 Million in 2025.
Europe accounted for about 21.8% (USD 577.82 Million).
Latin America represented approximately 4.0% of the market (USD 105.94 Million), while Mideast and Africa accounted for about 3.0% (USD 79.10 Million).

Entertainment and Roleplay led the worldwide AI companion app market in 2025, capturing nearly half of revenue share In 2025, Entertainment and Roleplay set the pace, reaching USD 1,192.72 Billion and accounting for an estimated 45.0% of worldwide AI companion app market share.
Emotional Support and Therapy followed, representing approximately 34.7% share with USD 919.60 Billion in 2025 revenue.

Virtual Assistant and Productivity rounded out the three largest categories, capturing about 20.3% share at USD 537.68 Billion in 2025, and it typically appeals to users who treat the companion as a daily tool for planning, reminders, and quick task support.

From 2026 to 2032, these cost pressures likely reward the segments that can pair engagement or utility with efficient deployment and predictable usage patterns [8] White House Announcement, March 2026 . iOS was the absolute market leader in 2025, accounting for USD 1,459.05 Million and representing approximately 55.1% of the global AI companion app market.
Android held the secondary position in 2025, contributing USD 1,190.95 Million and representing approximately 44.9% of the market.

records.title: Gaming Industry Emerges from Post-Pandemic Slump: 55% of Gamers Are Playing More in the Last Six Months
records.titleEn: Gaming Industry Emerges from Post-Pandemic Slump: 55% of Gamers Are Playing More in the Last Six Months
records.evidence:
BCG Report Projects Gaming Industry Revenues Will Hit $350 Billion by 2030 Cloud Gaming Revenue Will Reach $18.3 Billion by 2030, Up 57% from 2023 40% of Gamers Are Consuming More User-Generated Content Than Last Year BOSTON —The gaming industry is emerging from its post-pandemic slowdown, with global gaming revenue projected to grow by 6% from 2026 to 2030 and reach $350 billion by 2030.
AI can boost efficiency by improving code and automating quality assurance.
A new survey of approximately 3,000 gamers found that 55% of them increased their playing time during the past six months.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: BCG Report Projects Gaming Industry Revenues Will Hit $350 Billion by 2030 Cloud Gaming Revenue Will Reach $18.3 Billion by 2030, Up 57% from 2023 40% of Gamers Are Consuming More User-Generated Content Than Last Year BOSTON —The gaming industry is emerging from its post-pandemic slowdown, with global gaming revenue projected to grow by 6% from 2026 to 2030 and reach $350 billion by 2030.
A new survey of approximately 3,000 gamers found that 55% of them increased their playing time during the past six months.
UGC has emerged as a rapidly growing creator economy, with payouts that will reach $1.5 billion in 2025 from two games alone.
More than 40% of survey respondents said that they’re consuming more UGC this year than last year, but only 10% to 15% have created content themselves.
Although 60% of respondents said they had tried cloud gaming, and 80% reported a positive experience, only 27% of gamers said they are regular or heavy users of cloud gaming.
Still, cloud gaming revenues are set to grow from around $1.4 billion in 2025 to $18.3 billion in 2030, and the number of users will surpass 50 million.
BCG’s report estimates that mobile in-app purchases in 2025 will approach $130 billion, nearly half of global industry revenue.

records.title: In the gen AI economy, consumers want innovation they can trust
records.titleEn: In the gen AI economy, consumers want innovation they can trust
records.evidence:
Our survey finds that most surveyed consumers (53%) are now either experimenting with gen AI or using it regularly—up sharply from 38% in 2024 (figure 1).
1 Overall, tech affordability pressures appear to be easing slightly.
Deloitte Insights and our research centers deliver proprietary research designed to help organizations turn their aspirations into action.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Our survey finds that most surveyed consumers (53%) are now either experimenting with gen AI or using it regularly—up sharply from 38% in 2024 (figure 1).
Gen AI users—those who use it regularly for projects and tasks beyond experimentation—nearly doubled to 20% over the past year.
Roughly half of surveyed gen AI users (51%) say they use it every day, and 38% say they use it at least once a week, which suggests that gen AI is becoming part of their routine digital activities.
Deloitte’s 2025 Connected Consumer survey shows that US households spent an average of US$896 on connected devices in the past year—a significant uptick from US$764 in 2024.
Looking ahead, 29% of respondents say they plan to boost their device spending in the coming year—up threefold from 2023—while 24% say they’re looking to cut back on their device spending (figure 3).
In 2025, about half of respondents (51%) say they expect affordability challenges in the coming year, compared to 61% of respondents in 2024.

Among surveyed consumers, 23% expect to delay device purchases, 17% anticipate not being able to afford the more advanced devices their household wants, and 16% think they may cut back on tech services, subscriptions, or software.
Respondents report that their households spend an average of US$183 monthly on digital services, a slight uptick from US$175 in 2024.

The data suggests this upward trend is likely to continue: A quarter of survey respondents expect to increase their spending on tech services and subscriptions—a sharp jump from 14% who said the same last year.
Another 57% of respondents say they plan to keep their spending steady, down significantly from 72% last year.

Personal use leads gen AI adoption, but work-related use is growing fast Personal use remains the leading application of gen AI, cited by 85% of surveyed users and experimenters, while 22% say they use it for educational or school purposes.
Work-related use (among employed respondents) shows steady growth, climbing from 6% in 2023 to 34% in 2025 (figure 4).
Among those surveyed who are using gen AI for work, more than half (55%) say their organizations encourage its use, and 40% say their companies provide training.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: 68% prioritise AI features in next smartphone, but 82% say trust will decide the purchase: Report AI has overtaken design, price and battery life in purchase priorities, while consumers increasingly demand transparent data practices and on-device AI processing.

A new study by CyberMedia Research (CMR) found that 68% of consumers now prioritise AI capabilities when evaluating smartphones, while 82% said transparent data practices are essential for trusting AI-powered experiences.
The study found that 61% of respondents believe on-device AI processing improves both responsiveness and privacy, indicating growing awareness of how AI functions on smartphones.
Performance remains the most important consideration for smartphone buyers, cited by 78% of respondents, followed by camera quality, including AI enhancements (70%), and AI features (59%).

When choosing between similarly priced devices, 60% of consumers said they prefer a smartphone that offers both strong AI capabilities and powerful hardware, while 25% described themselves as AI-first buyers.
The trend is particularly strong among younger consumers, with 72% of Gen Z respondents saying AI will influence their next smartphone purchase, compared with 65% of millennials.

AI-powered photography continues to be the most widely used application, with 77% of respondents regularly using features such as low-light enhancement, portrait optimisation and intelligent scene detection.
While 66% of female consumers primarily use AI for camera and imaging features, 42% of male respondents prioritise productivity and communication use cases.
CMR also referenced its India Mobile Handset Market Review Report, which found that MediaTek accounted for 47% of smartphone chipset shipments in India.
The survey additionally reported that 93% of MediaTek users expressed satisfaction with their devices, while more than 45% said they would prefer a MediaTek-powered smartphone.

records.title: Dentsu Digital survey finds 57% use AI for travel planning
records.titleEn: Dentsu Digital survey finds 57% use AI for travel planning
records.evidence:
Valid responses totaled 10,000 for the screening survey and 3,300 for the main survey.
Its first survey, titled "Consumer AI Usage Survey 2026.7," examined how AI is being used in purchasing behavior and decision-making.
Dentsu Digital said the findings show AI use is spreading in awareness, comparison and post-purchase phases, while people still account for a higher share of decision-making at the final stage.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Dentsu Digital survey finds 57% use AI for travel planning

Dentsu Digital launches with AI Lab and publishes a July 2026 survey on consumer AI use in purchasing About one in three private AI users consult AI before purchases, with travel and financial categories above 50% AI use is strongest in awareness, comparison and post-purchase stages, while final buying decisions remain more human-led Dentsu Digital said on July 23 that about one in three consumers who use artificial intelligence in their private lives had consulted AI about purchases made within the past six months, releasing the first findings from a new in-house research unit focused on consumer behavior in the AI era.

The ratio was highest in higher-involvement categories where consumers tend to compare options more closely, with 57% in travel planning and accommodation bookings and 56% in financial products and insurance.

Across product categories, 2% to 3% of respondents said they adopted AI responses as-is for their final decision, indicating that some consumers are beginning to leave the ultimate purchase choice to AI.

records.title: Only 45% of marketers gain quality from AI, WARC and TikTok find
records.titleEn: Only 45% of marketers gain quality from AI, WARC and TikTok find
records.evidence:
A MiQ survey from November 2025, reported by PPC Land , found 72% of marketers planning AI adoption growth while only 45% felt confident.
by Luis Rijo Luis Rijo Luís Rijo is a seasoned marketing professional with over 10 years of experience in Digital Marketing, Search, Social, Display, Video, and DOOH.
A Taboola study across a publisher network of roughly 600 million daily active users found AI-generated creatives increased or maintained click-through rates without damaging conversion rates , with strongest results in food and drink and personal finance and more muted outcomes in categories such as education.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Only 45% of marketers gain quality from AI, WARC and TikTok find
by Luis Rijo Luis Rijo Luís Rijo is a seasoned marketing professional with over 10 years of experience in Digital Marketing, Search, Social, Display, Video, and DOOH.

According to the survey, 90% of marketers agree generative AI has become a key tool in the creative development process, 72% use it frequently as a regular part of content production, and 87% believe their organisation is using it effectively for creative development.
WARC's Marketer's Toolkit found that 59% of marketers agree traditional demographic segmentation is no longer effective.
Yet the new survey found demographic data remains the primary input used to brief AI, relied on by 67% of respondents.
Only 17% of marketers make it a rule to always incorporate community or audience insights beyond demographics into generative AI workflows.

Asked to identify the biggest gaps in inputs currently available when briefing generative AI, respondents pointed first to audience behavioural data covering how people engage rather than who they are, cited by 45%.
Access to real-time cultural or community signals and tools that translate insights into effective AI briefs each registered 35%.
Only 10% of respondents said they do not perceive significant gaps in the inputs available to them.

According to the survey, 86% of marketers agree audience behaviour and community signals will influence creative development significantly more over the next three years, and one in three believe access to richer audience or cultural signals would do most to unlock generative AI advantage.

A Taboola study across a publisher network of roughly 600 million daily active users found AI-generated creatives increased or maintained click-through rates without damaging conversion rates , with strongest results in food and drink and personal finance and more muted outcomes in categories such as education.
The WARC and TikTok figure of 87% of marketers believing their organisation uses generative AI effectively sits awkwardly against other industry measurement.
A MiQ survey from November 2025, reported by PPC Land , found 72% of marketers planning AI adoption growth while only 45% felt confident.
The same MIQ Global AI Confidence Curve is cited inside the WARC report itself for a separate finding: only 40% of marketers strongly believe they can apply findings from one campaign to another.
A self-reported 87% effectiveness rating from a vendor-commissioned survey and a 45% confidence rating from an independent one describe the same industry.
Brandwatch survey findings reported in April 2026 identified social listening and consumer research as a top skill gap at 55%, with cross-platform content optimisation at 52%.

records.title: Foldable smartphones are moving into a pivotal 2026
records.titleEn: Foldable smartphones are moving into a pivotal 2026
records.evidence:
The second-largest foldable market, the US, grew modestly by 7% in H1 2025, driven mainly by Motorola’s Razr 2025 series.
They are a proving ground for whether hardware R&D can still deliver meaningful differentiation in an industry where the gravitational pull is shifting toward software, artificial intelligence, and services as the core revenue drivers.
Consequently, the scale and wider strategic relevance of foldable smartphones is moving up the priority list.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Even though the category is more crowded, global shipments were flat at 6.6 million units in H1 2025.
China was the major exception, growing 32.8% year-on-year, predominantly driven by Huawei’s Mate and Pura X models.
The second-largest foldable market, the US, grew modestly by 7% in H1 2025, driven mainly by Motorola’s Razr 2025 series.
Even though vendors are experiencing above-expected momentum with their recent launches, global foldable shipments are forecast to remain flat at 17.2 million units for the full year.
Omdia forecasts foldable smartphone shipments to grow by a staggering 50% YoY in 2026 and carry momentum into 2027.
Foldables remain a niche in shipment terms, making up between 1.0-1.5% of global volumes and only 5% of devices priced above US$700.
One Galaxy Z Fold7 sold at list price (around US$1899) generates the equivalent revenue of roughly 15 entry-level Galaxy A06 4Gs.
In 2024, only 15% of Samsung’s smartphones sold worldwide were priced above US$1,000 (Galaxy S and Z).
However, these devices contributed a staggering 44% of shipment value.
Within that tier, foldables (Galaxy Z and W) contributed more than 20% of volume, helping lift ASPs and shift Samsung’s revenue mix away from the low-margin, hyper- competitive mass market.

In a recent consumer study conducted by Omdia across five global markets (N=5000) that focused on cutting-edge smartphone tech, 96% of respondents showed some level of familiarity with foldable smartphones.

However, almost 40% of respondents said they were not interested in foldable smartphones, and over a third of respondents stated they were interested but foldables sit outside their budget or don’t meet their needs.

records.evidence:
Omdia estimates that cellular standard devices, meaning smartphones using 4G or 5G technologies to connect directly to satellites, will become the dominant model in the smartphone satellite D2D market, accounting for over 95% of global total MAUs by 2030.
This represents mean annual growth rates of 80.1% for users and 49.4% for revenue from 2026 to 2030.
“In contrast to dual-mode phone solutions, which require a proprietary satellite communication link in the smartphone, cellular standard based solutions, such as Starlink D2C and AST SpaceMobile, can directly connect to devices compliant with 4G or 5G standards, particularly existing smartphones,” noted Guang Yang, Senior Principal Analyst, Service Provider Strategies and Mobile Infrastructure, at Omdia .

records.evidence:

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Forecast: Consumer agentic AI will soar to $3.3tn in 2030
Forecast: Consumer agentic AI will soar to $3.3tn in 2030 Marketing is operating in an age of abundance.
The study finds that total agent-facilitated consumer spending will triple from $944 billion (€827.7bn) this year to $3.35 trillion in 2030.

James McDonald, Director of Data, Intelligence & Forecasting, WARC, and author of the research, added: “This landmark study finds that agentic AI is already facilitating the path to purchase for many consumers, and will become deeply embedded over the coming years to influence $3.35 trillion in household expenditure by 2030.

US: The US will lead agentic AI spending at $1.1 trillion (31.9 per cent of the global total), driven by consumers already comfortable with digital commerce and brands with the resources to deploy agents at scale.

China: China will be the second-largest market at $505.8 billion (15.1 per cent of global spend), powered by high platform integration, government support, and consumers ready to embrace delegated commerce.
UK: The UK will capture 3.9 per cent of global agentic AI spending ($131.2 billion), driven by strong talent, major investments, and government backing for AI-led transformation.
Telecoms & Utilities will grow 611.9 per cent from $57.6 billion in 2026 to $410.3 billion by 2030 – making it the largest category for AI agents.
Total agent-facilitated consumer spending will increase 235.3 per cent to $237.9 billion by 2030.
Travel & Transport will lead agent-facilitated spending at $78.1 billion in 2026, surging 252.8 per cent to $275.6 billion by 2030 as AI agents take control of discovery, planning, and booking.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: New Delhi: A majority of young Indians are using artificial intelligence (AI) beyond work and productivity, with over 70% seeking career advice from AI tools and nearly half saying their daily lives would be disrupted if they lost access to AI for a week, according to a study by PulseAI Research, the consumer insights division of Smytten.

The report, titled 'The AI Companion Report: How Young Indians Are Learning, Working, and Making Decisions with AI', surveyed more than 2,000 respondents across India, most of them aged between 18 and 34 years.
According to the study, 70.6% of respondents have already used AI for career advice, while 62% said they would be comfortable using it for career coaching in the future.
The report found that 41.4% of respondents now turn to AI before using search engines when looking for information online.

records.title: Intel Q2 2026 Revenue Surges 25% as AI Server Chips, Foundry Business and PC Demand Fuel Strongest Growth in 15 Years - InfotechLead
records.titleEn: Intel Q2 2026 Revenue Surges 25% as AI Server Chips, Foundry Business and PC Demand Fuel Strongest Growth in 15 Years - InfotechLead
records.evidence:
Intel reported Q2 2026 revenue of $16.1 billion, an increase of 25 percent, significantly above its guidance range of $14.4 billion to $15.4 billion.
Intel’s Client Computing and Physical AI Group (CCPG) delivered $6.3 billion in revenue with 13 percent increase as demand shifted toward premium AI-enabled PCs.
Intel delivered its strongest quarterly revenue growth in more than 15 years during the second quarter of 2026, driven by surging demand for AI infrastructure, data center processors, premium PC chips and expanding foundry services.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Intel Q2 2026 Revenue Surges 25% as AI Server Chips, Foundry Business and PC Demand Fuel Strongest Growth in 15 Years - InfotechLead

Intel delivered its strongest quarterly revenue growth in more than 15 years during the second quarter of 2026, driven by surging demand for AI infrastructure, data center processors, premium PC chips and expanding foundry services.
Intel reported Q2 2026 revenue of $16.1 billion, an increase of 25 percent, significantly above its guidance range of $14.4 billion to $15.4 billion.
Revenue surged 59 percent to $6.3 billion, supported by adoption of Xeon 6 processors, increasing AI server deployments and rising demand for CPUs powering agentic AI workloads.
Intel’s Client Computing and Physical AI Group (CCPG) delivered $6.3 billion in revenue with 13 percent increase as demand shifted toward premium AI-enabled PCs.
Omdia said more than half of B2B channel partners reported customers postponing hardware refresh plans until market conditions stabilize, while 6 percent expect outright cancellations.
Intel Foundry generated $5.8 billion in revenue, representing 31 percent growth.

Reflecting confidence in future demand, Intel increased its planned 2026 capital expenditure to $20 billion, up from earlier expectations, to expand manufacturing capacity and meet rising AI-driven processor demand.

The company ended the quarter with approximately $30 billion in cash and investments, supported by an additional $10 billion credit facility that provides financial flexibility for manufacturing expansion and technology investments.
Looking ahead, Intel forecast third-quarter 2026 revenue between $15.8 billion and $16.8 billion.

records.title: Disability Consumer Market Hits $675 Billion, Creating Growth Opportunity for Businesses
records.titleEn: Disability Consumer Market Hits $675 Billion, Creating Growth Opportunity for Businesses
records.evidence:
The US disability consumer market has grown to an estimated $675 billion, according to a major new study from Disability:IN and the American Institutes for Research (AIR), highlighting a significant commercial opportunity for businesses that invest in accessibility, inclusive products and disability-focused customer strategies.
The report, The Next Growth Market: Inside the $675 Billion Consumer Opportunity , examines the purchasing power of working-age adults with disabilities (aged 16–64) and argues that businesses across every sector stand to benefit by designing products, services and customer experiences that better meet the needs of disabled consumers.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Disability Consumer Market Hits $675 Billion, Creating Growth Opportunity for Businesses

New research reveals that people with disabilities now account for nearly 7% of US disposable income, with $107 billion in annual discretionary spending, highlighting one of the world’s largest – and most overlooked – consumer markets.

The US disability consumer market has grown to an estimated $675 billion, according to a major new study from Disability:IN and the American Institutes for Research (AIR), highlighting a significant commercial opportunity for businesses that invest in accessibility, inclusive products and disability-focused customer strategies.

The report, The Next Growth Market: Inside the $675 Billion Consumer Opportunity , examines the purchasing power of working-age adults with disabilities (aged 16–64) and argues that businesses across every sector stand to benefit by designing products, services and customer experiences that better meet the needs of disabled consumers.
As previously reported, research has estimated the global disability market to be worth US$13 trillion in annual spending power , making it one of the world’s largest consumer segments.
The report estimates that the disability consumer market is now worth $675 billion, equivalent in size to the global beauty and cosmetics industry.
Annual discretionary income across the disability community has reached $107 billion.
Approximately 10% of working-age people with disabilities have an average $40,000 in discretionary spending power each year.
Those consumers have an average pre-tax income of $135,805, reflecting a growing segment with significant purchasing power.

“The opportunity presented by the $675 billion disability consumer market is enormous, especially for businesses that develop accessible products, emerge as the brand of choice by capturing everyday consumer dollars and include people with disabilities in their go-to-market strategies.”
The study found that: Average disposable income for people with disabilities is approximately $40,000 per year.
Average disposable income for people without disabilities is around $68,000 annually.

“If the momentum achieved over the past 10 years is any indication of what the future holds, then we can project with confidence that the favourable trends identified in our research will bear brighter tomorrows for the disability community, businesses at large and the US economy overall.”

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: According to Avalara's report, Agents of Change: How the Race to Deploy AI Agents Is Outrunning Financial Governance, 85% of Indian finance leaders say they face moderate or significant career pressure to prove that AI agent investments are generating returns.
The survey also found that 71% believe the focus inside their organizations is on deploying AI agents quickly, while only 8% say governance takes priority over speed.

The report suggests governance frameworks have yet to catch up with the pace of AI adoption. 27% of Indian respondents said accountability for significant AI agent errors is either unclear or assigned to no one, the highest share among respondents in India, the US, the UK, and Australia. 24% have not updated internal controls in the past year to reflect AI-driven decisions.

Only 28% say AI controls have been reviewed by IT or cybersecurity teams. 10% are not confident they could clearly explain an AI agent's decisions to regulators or auditors, a higher share than respondents in the US, the UK, and Australia.
The survey also found that 76% of Indian finance leaders lack dedicated in-house expertise to fully understand how their AI agents work.

records.title: AI Infrastructure Spending Holds Near $90 Billion in Q1 2026 as ARM Overtakes x86 in Accelerated Servers; 2026 Forecast Raised to $497 Billion
records.titleEn: AI Infrastructure Spending Holds Near $90 Billion in Q1 2026 as ARM Overtakes x86 in Accelerated Servers; 2026 Forecast Raised to $497 Billion
records.evidence:
According to IDC's Worldwide Quarterly AI Infrastructure Tracker, spending reached $89.7 billion in Q1 2026, up 33% year-over-year but flat sequentially as growth normalizes off a larger base.
Server spending represented 97.6% of total AI infrastructure value in Q1 2026, and within that, a growing share of AI-centric demand is landing on infrastructure that isn’t GPU-accelerated at all.
For vendors, this means a prolonged period of elevated demand across accelerated compute, high-performance storage, and supporting network infrastructure, but also a fast-moving contest for architecture leadership, as ARM rackscale platforms displace x86 in the accelerated server market.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: AI Infrastructure Spending Holds Near $90 Billion in Q1 2026 as ARM Overtakes x86 in Accelerated Servers; 2026 Forecast Raised to $497 Billion
According to IDC's Worldwide Quarterly AI Infrastructure Tracker, spending reached $89.7 billion in Q1 2026, up 33% year-over-year but flat sequentially as growth normalizes off a larger base.
IDC raised its full-year 2026 forecast to $497 billion on hyperscaler capex growth and emerging non-GPU AI demand.
IDC now projects the global AI infrastructure market will surpass $1 trillion in 2029, reaching $1.08 trillion, before climbing to $1.21 trillion in 2030.
The United States remained dominant at $67.9 billion (75.7% of global spend, +30.3% YoY), though growth continues to moderate.
China (PRC) returned to growth at $7.8 billion (8.7% share, +9.3% YoY).
The Middle East & Africa remained the fastest-growing region (+233% YoY to $1.1 billion), followed by APeJC (+62% to $5.8 billion) and Western Europe (up to $5.1 billion).
Server spending represented 97.6% of total AI infrastructure value in Q1 2026, and within that, a growing share of AI-centric demand is landing on infrastructure that isn’t GPU-accelerated at all.

Pent-up storage refresh is now landing on top of genuine AI-driven demand, reinforcing the urgency behind external storage strategy even as AI-centric storage remains a small share (2.4%) of total AI infrastructure value.

We watched x86 accelerated servers fall from $52 billion to $35 billion in just two quarters while ARM rack-scale platforms nearly doubled, and that’s not demand destruction, that’s an architecture shift that is yet to be definitive as new x86 platforms are on the horizon as well.
Q1 2026’s 33% year-over-year growth reflects a much higher base, not a slowdown in demand.

Yes, Non-x86 (ARM) accelerated server value climbed to $53.0 billion in Q1 2026, up from $47.5 billion in Q4 2025 and $29.8 billion in Q3 2025, while x86 accelerated value fell to $34.6 billion from $42.7 billion and $51.9 billion over the same span.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: IDC: Global AI Infrastructure Spending Hits $89.7 Billion in Q1 2026, ARM Servers Overtake x86 as Market Heads Toward $1.21 Trillion by 2030 - InfotechLead

Global spending on AI infrastructure reached $89.7 billion in the first quarter of 2026, representing a 33.1 percent increase year on year, according to IDC’s Worldwide Quarterly AI Infrastructure Tracker.

IDC has raised its full-year 2026 AI infrastructure spending forecast to $497 billion, reflecting continued hyperscaler capital expenditure, growing enterprise adoption, and rising demand for AI infrastructure beyond GPU-based computing.
The global AI infrastructure market will exceed $1.08 trillion in 2029 before reaching $1.21 trillion in 2030, representing a five-year CAGR of approximately 30 percent from 2025.

IDC reported that non-x86 (ARM) accelerated servers generated $53.0 billion in spending during the quarter, compared with $34.6 billion for x86 systems, highlighting a significant shift in AI data center deployments, Juan Seminara, Research Director, Worldwide Infrastructure Trackers, IDC, said in a blog post .
Server infrastructure dominated AI spending, accounting for $87.6 billion, or 97.6 percent of total AI infrastructure investment.
Storage spending reached $2.2 billion, representing 2.4 percent of the market.

United States Maintains Leadership While Middle East Records Fastest Growth The United States remained the world’s largest AI infrastructure market with $67.9 billion in spending during Q1 2026, representing 75.7 percent of global investment and growing 30.3 percent year over year.
China returned to growth with $7.8 billion, accounting for 8.7 percent of worldwide spending and expanding 9.3 percent compared with a year earlier.

The Middle East and Africa emerged as the fastest-growing region globally, with spending increasing 233 percent year over year to $1.1 billion, supported by sovereign AI initiatives and government-backed investments.

Asia Pacific excluding Japan and China (APeJC) region recorded 62 percent growth to $5.8 billion, while Western Europe reached $5.1 billion as governments and enterprises accelerated AI infrastructure deployment.

AI Infrastructure Spending Continues Multi-Year Expansion Global AI infrastructure spending reached $318 billion in 2025, more than doubling from $153 billion in 2024, which itself represented 107.6 percent year-over-year growth.
AI infrastructure spending will expand by approximately 56 percent in 2026, an upward revision from its previous estimate of around 53 percent growth.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Gartner predicts AI models and platforms spend to hit US$64B - ARN

Worldwide end-user spending on AI models and platforms is projected to total US$64 billion in 2026, up 63.4 per cent from US$39 billion in 2025, with more and more enterprises are choosing to work with companies that can provide clear value.

Spending on generative AI (genAI) models is forecast to grow 117 per cent while AI platform spending will rise 36.9 per cent in 2026, according to Gartner’s latest forecast on AI platforms and models. “Enterprise AI budgets are coming under greater scrutiny, with increased focus on usage efficiency, cost control and measurable outcomes ,” said the analyst firm’s senior principal research analyst, Arunasree Cheparthi. “Spending is shifting toward providers who can demonstrate clear value across cost, latency, performance, and reliability. “This is giving an edge to providers that embed evaluation, cost transparency, and usage tracking into customer workflows, making it easier to manage and optimise AI use.” However, as spending becomes more usage-driven, providers face pressure to demonstrate real adoption, sustained use, and durable margins.
This dynamic is accelerating growth in domain-specific language models (DSLMs) and specialised models, which are forecast to grow 210 percent in 2026.

According to Gartner, the AI software market is forecast to grow significantly between 2025 and 2026, with total market revenue increasing from US$39.3 billion to US$64.3 billion, representing 63.4 per cent growth.
The Foundation Generative AI Models segment is expected to more than double, rising from US$11.4 billion in 2025 to US$23.4 billion in 2026, representing a growth rate of 104.2 per cent.
Meanwhile, the fastest-growing segment is DSLMs and specialised genAI models, which is projected to expand from US$1.6 billion to US$4.9 billion, achieving 210.0 per cent growth.

AI application development platforms are forecast to grow from US$6.9 billion to US$9.5 billion (up 38.6 per cent), and AI platforms for data science and machine learning are expected to increase from US$19.4 billion to US$26.4 billion (an increase of 36.3 per cent).

Overall, these projections highlight accelerating investment in generative AI technologies, particularly in specialised AI and foundation models . “Over the long-term, the biggest winners will be vendors that help enterprises manage where and how AI is used across the business ,” said Cheparthi. “As more models enter the market and usage-based pricing becomes harder to predict, buyers will turn to platforms that help them choose the right tools, monitor performance , enforce policy and keep costs under control.” Equinix passes top Australian leadership to Jarrod Nink Cohesity promotes Peter Hanna to lead growth in Asia Pacific and Japan As White House monitors latest OpenAI incident, Congress eyes an AI ‘kill switch’ for DHS news EDGE 2026: Becoming the successful MSP for the future 28 Jul 2026 6 mins news EDGE 2026: The MSP of the future 27 Jul 2026 4 mins news AI data centre growth ignites debate over power, water, and infrastructure 27 Jul 2026 11 mins news Monvia lists on ASX after $17.5M IPO 24 Jul 2026 2 mins news SoftwareOne adds NinjaOne to portfolio 24 Jul 2026 2 mins news Adactin teams up with Cyara to support AI-powered customer service 23 Jul 2026 2 mins news Synnex strengthens Microsoft practice with four Microsoft specialisations 23 Jul 2026 3 mins news Datacom considers next steps for local MD role as Laura Malcolm departs 22 Jul 2026 3 mins Leading Edge DC hires Schneider Electric’s Joe Craparotta as CEO Ingram Micro Australia added to Oracle’s Cloud Distribution Program

It highlighted that spending on generative AI (GenAI) models is expected to grow 117 per cent in 2026, while spending on AI platforms is forecast to increase 36.9 per cent during the year.
According to the forecast, spending on Foundation Generative AI Models will increase from USD 11.4 billion in 2025 to USD 23.4 billion in 2026, registering a growth of 104.2 per cent.

The report also projected spending on AI Application Development Platforms to increase from USD 6.9 billion in 2025 to USD 9.5 billion in 2026, while spending on AI Platforms for Data Science and Machine Learning is expected to rise from USD 19.4 billion to USD 26.4 billion during the same period.

records.titleEn: AI Coding Tools Hit $9B as Pricing Goes Metered
records.evidence:
Coding has become the most contested benchmark in AI, and the tools built on top of frontier models are absorbing real inference costs that a $10 or $20 monthly subscription increasingly cannot cover.
GitHub moved Copilot onto usage-based billing, charging for premium requests once a plan’s included allowance runs out, at a rate of roughly $0.04 per request under the current schedule.
Enterprise software spent the 2010s moving from perpetual licences to per-seat SaaS subscriptions, another shift driven by vendors needing revenue that tracked usage more closely than a one-time sale ever could.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: AI Coding Tools Hit $9B as Pricing Goes Metered

Coding has become the most contested benchmark in AI, and the tools built on top of frontier models are absorbing real inference costs that a $10 or $20 monthly subscription increasingly cannot cover.
Mordor Intelligence sizes the global AI code tools market at roughly $9.35 billion in 2026, expanding at more than 26% a year.
GitHub moved Copilot onto usage-based billing, charging for premium requests once a plan’s included allowance runs out, at a rate of roughly $0.04 per request under the current schedule.
Copilot Pro still lists at $10 a month and Copilot Enterprise at $39 per user per month, but both now sit on top of a metered layer that tracks actual usage rather than assuming it away.

GitHub’s own research previously found that Copilot users complete tasks about 55% faster than developers coding without it, a strong pitch for adoption but a rough one for margins once millions of developers start running agentic workflows against the same infrastructure.
A flat $20 monthly subscription only works if the average user’s token consumption stays well below what that fee actually covers.
That behaviour is a major reason Claude Code was reported to author close to 4% of all public GitHub commits by early 2026, a figure some analysts expect to pass 20% before the year is out.
The spread between roughly $9 billion and $34 billion for the same year comes down to scope.

Taking the narrower, more comparable estimates from Mordor Intelligence, Grand View Research, and Research and Markets, the market sits close to $9 to $10 billion in 2026 and is on track for somewhere between $19 billion and $26 billion by 2030.

Surveys circulating in early 2026 put Claude Code’s “most loved” rating among senior engineers at 46%, against 19% for Cursor and 9% for GitHub Copilot, and separate JetBrains-linked data credits Claude Code with a 91% customer satisfaction score and a net promoter score of 54, the highest reported in the category.

In startups under 50 employees, Claude Code adoption reportedly reaches 75% against 42% for Cursor, while GitHub Copilot holds a commanding 56% share inside companies with more than 10,000 employees, largely on the back of existing Microsoft procurement relationships.
Copilot’s installed base remains enormous regardless, with more than 15 million developers across upwards of 77,000 organisations, including a reported 77% of the Fortune 500.

TSMC reported 77 percent year-on-year increase in net profit to a record T$706.6 billion (approximately $22 billion), significantly exceeding market expectations.
The 2nm process contributed 3 percent, 3nm accounted for 30 percent, and technologies 7nm and below represented 77 percent of total wafer revenue, highlighting the industry’s rapid transition toward leading-edge nodes for AI and high-performance computing workloads.
The strong financial performance was driven by sustained demand for advanced semiconductor technologies, including 3nm and 2nm process nodes and advanced CoWoS chip packaging, which are critical for AI accelerators and high-performance computing applications.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: TSMC Q2 2026 Profit Soars 77% to Record T$706.6 bn as AI Chip Demand Drives Growth and Capex Rises - TelecomLead
TSMC reported 77 percent year-on-year increase in net profit to a record T$706.6 billion (approximately $22 billion), significantly exceeding market expectations.

High Performance Computing (HPC) remained TSMC’s largest business segment, contributing 66 percent of total revenue as demand for AI GPUs, AI accelerators and custom processors from major customers such as Nvidia, AMD, Apple and Broadcom continued to surge.
TSMC’s smartphone business accounted for 22 percent of revenue despite seasonal softness.
TSMC’s Internet of Things (IoT) segment contributed 6 percent.
Automotive represented 3 percent of revenue, Digital Consumer Electronics (DCE) generated 1 percent, and other businesses contributed the remaining 2 percent.

The 2nm process contributed 3 percent, 3nm accounted for 30 percent, and technologies 7nm and below represented 77 percent of total wafer revenue, highlighting the industry’s rapid transition toward leading-edge nodes for AI and high-performance computing workloads.
The latest Omdia report said global smartphone shipments dropped 4 percent in 2Q26 as the memory crisis disrupted supply and pushed up component costs.
Apple, one of the main customers of TSMC, has increased its smartphone market share to 20 percent in Q2 2026 from 16 percent in Q2 2025.
Geographically, North America generated 78 percent of TSMC’s revenue in the second quarter, underlining the company’s growing dependence on U.S. hyperscale cloud providers and AI chip designers.
Asia Pacific accounted for 8 percent, China contributed 6 percent, while Japan and Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA) each represented 4 percent of total revenue.
TSMC also maintained a positive outlook, forecasting more than 40 percent revenue growth for full-year 2026, supported by robust AI infrastructure investments from global technology companies.
Reflecting confidence in long-term AI demand, TSMC increased its 2026 capital expenditure guidance to between $60 billion and $64 billion, up from its earlier upper-end estimate of $56 billion.
The company also announced an additional $100 billion investment in Arizona, expanding its total planned U.S. investment to $265 billion.

TSMC’s market capitalization has climbed to approximately $1.97 trillion, nearly double that of Samsung Electronics, underscoring its dominant position in the global semiconductor industry, Reuters news report said.

records.title: 60% of agentic AI costs go to response refinement, and most enterprises are already over budget
records.titleEn: 60% of agentic AI costs go to response refinement, and most enterprises are already over budget
records.evidence:
If 60 percent of the bill sits in refinement loops rather than primary inference, and most budget frameworks were built around inference costs alone, the gap between forecast and actual spend will widen as agentic deployments scale.
The findings from its May 2026 FinOps survey already suggest that the budget conversation has moved from the IT team to the C-suite, and it is unlikely to move back.
McKinsey's July 2026 report, published in the McKinsey Quarterly and authored by researchers from QuantumBlack, AI by McKinsey, pinpoints response refinement as the dominant cost driver: 60 percent of total agentic AI spend goes not to the first inference call but to the iterative cycles of checking, correcting, and improving that agents run before delivering a usable output.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Inference on GPT-3.5-level capability cost $20 per million tokens in early 2024 and fell to $0.07 by year's end, according to the Stanford HAI 2025 AI Index cited in McKinsey's new report.

LLM expenditures tripled over a 12-month period by the end of 2025, according to a Menlo Ventures study also cited by McKinsey, and 93 percent of organizations surveyed by McKinsey in May 2026 reported exceeding their AI budgets.

McKinsey's July 2026 report, published in the McKinsey Quarterly and authored by researchers from QuantumBlack, AI by McKinsey, pinpoints response refinement as the dominant cost driver: 60 percent of total agentic AI spend goes not to the first inference call but to the iterative cycles of checking, correcting, and improving that agents run before delivering a usable output.
McKinsey's Enterprise AI FinOps Survey, conducted in May 2026 with 75 qualified respondents across five major industries, found that 93 percent have already blown past their AI budgets.

records.title: Google's $205 Billion AI Bet Terrified Investors. Here's Why the Market Was Wrong
records.titleEn: Google's $205 Billion AI Bet Terrified Investors. Here's Why the Market Was Wrong
records.evidence:
Alphabet's first-ever negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion masked Google Cloud's 82% revenue surge to $24.8 billion with operating margins tripling.
According to Alphabet’s earnings, Google is already converting AI investment into accelerating cloud revenue, expanding margins, and posting a record $514 billion backlog waiting to become future sales.
A record $514 billion signed cloud backlog means much of Alphabet's $205 billion capex is effectively pre-sold before the infrastructure even goes live.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Google's $205 Billion AI Bet Terrified Investors. Here's Why the Market Was Wrong
Alphabet's first-ever negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion masked Google Cloud's 82% revenue surge to $24.8 billion with operating margins tripling.
A record $514 billion signed cloud backlog means much of Alphabet's $205 billion capex is effectively pre-sold before the infrastructure even goes live.
Free cash flow came in at negative $5.9 billion, a stunning reversal driven by an unprecedented surge in AI infrastructure spending.
Capital expenditures totaled $44.9 billion during the quarter, doubling from a year ago.
Even more surprising, management raised its 2026 capital expenditure forecast to $205 billion, signaling that spending is still accelerating rather than slowing.
Collectively, the industry’s largest AI builders are on pace to spend well over $700 billion in 2026.
Google Cloud revenue jumped 82% year over year to $24.8 billion.
Perhaps the most overlooked figure was Google’s $514 billion cloud backlog — signed customer contracts that haven’t yet been recognized as revenue.
Wall Street currently forecasts 23% revenue growth this year followed by 21% next year.
If Alphabet maintains roughly 20% annual growth into 2028, the company would exit that year generating approximately $2 billion in revenue every single day.

According to Alphabet’s earnings, Google is already converting AI investment into accelerating cloud revenue, expanding margins, and posting a record $514 billion backlog waiting to become future sales.

But if Alphabet continues executing at its current pace, today’s $205 billion investment program may eventually look less like reckless spending and more like the foundation of its next long-term competitive moat.

records.title: ChatGPT Market Share Falls to 46.4% [2026]
records.titleEn: ChatGPT Market Share Falls to 46.4% [2026]
records.evidence:
Analytics provider Apptopia, first reported by Big Technology and later covered by Fortune , tracked ChatGPT’s app market share falling from 69.1% in January 2025 to 45.3% earlier in 2026, while Gemini’s app share rose from 14.7% to 25.2% across the same window.
The shift shows up just as clearly in Australia.
ChatGPT’s share of the market is shrinking while its user base and revenue keep climbing, because the overall AI-assistant market is expanding faster than ChatGPT alone can capture.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: ChatGPT Market Share Falls to 46.4% [2026]

Sensor Tower’s State of AI 2026 report puts OpenAI’s chatbot at 46.4% of the global AI-assistant market at the end of May 2026, the first time it has held less than half the market since debuting in November 2022.
Google’s Gemini climbed to 27.7% over the same period, and Anthropic’s Claude reached 10.3%, according to the same tracking data reported by TechCrunch on June 16, 2026 .

ChatGPT’s Market Share Falls Below 50% for the First Time The Numbers Behind the Slide: Three Trackers, One Story Claude’s Enterprise Play: How Anthropic Is Cutting Into OpenAI’s Lead Australia’s AI Adoption Numbers: Telsyte’s June 2026 Snapshot Market Share vs Revenue: Why OpenAI Still Leads on Money Competitive Comparison: ChatGPT vs Gemini vs Claude at a Glance Historical Context: How Fast Tech Leaders Usually Lose Ground What This Means for Australian Businesses Choosing an AI Vendor Market Impact: Why Investors and Analysts Are Watching Closely Five Predictions: Where AI Assistant Market Share Goes Next Does ChatGPT’s falling market share mean it’s losing users?

Telsyte’s June 2026 research counts more than 17 million Australians using AI tools monthly, but ChatGPT’s local lead is narrowing too: 13.8 million users against Gemini’s 9.1 million and Claude’s 2.9 million, per Telsyte’s announcement .
By that measure, ChatGPT’s global AI-assistant market share slipped under the 50% mark in March 2026 and kept falling, landing at 46.4% by the end of May.
A year earlier, in December 2024, ChatGPT held 65.3% of the same market.

Analytics provider Apptopia, first reported by Big Technology and later covered by Fortune , tracked ChatGPT’s app market share falling from 69.1% in January 2025 to 45.3% earlier in 2026, while Gemini’s app share rose from 14.7% to 25.2% across the same window.

Google folded Gemini into Search, Android, and Workspace rather than asking users to go find and install a separate app, and that bundling shows up directly in the numbers: Gemini’s monthly active users reached 662 million by May 2026, up from a 6% market share in early 2025 to 27.7% by May.
Paid conversion sits at a modest 3.1%, far behind Claude’s rate, which tells you Gemini’s growth is coming from reach rather than from users paying for premium tiers.
Claude’s consumer numbers look small next to ChatGPT and Gemini: 245 million monthly active users and 10.3% of the assistant market in May 2026.
The research firm counts Australia’s total AI user base at more than 17 million people, with 80% of them engaging monthly rather than trying a tool once and dropping it.

OpenAI’s weekly active users crossed 900 million on February 27, 2026, and monthly active users passed 1 billion in June 2026, making ChatGPT the fastest app in history to reach that milestone, according to Sensor Tower data reported by TechCrunch.
Annualized revenue crossed $25 billion by February 2026, up from roughly $20 billion in 2025 and $6 billion in 2024.
Mobile app revenue alone hit $1.35 billion in 2025, up 673% year over year from $174 million in 2024.

Roughly $25 billion in annualized revenue against 1.1 billion monthly users works out to an implied $20-something per user per year, though the real split is far more concentrated: a smaller base of paying subscribers and enterprise API customers accounts for most of that revenue, not the free-tier majority.

The shift shows up just as clearly in Australia.

records.titleEn: OpenAI Financials Leaked Ahead Of IPO? ChatGPT Maker Said To Have Lost $39B Last Year: Here's How That Compares To Anthropic, SpaceX
records.evidence:
The ChatGPT maker spent $34 billion last year, including $19 billion on research and development and nearly $6 billion on sales, marketing, and other expenses, according to the report .
The majority of the increase in net loss last year was due to non-cash accounting charges tied to the company’s prior structure rather than its underlying operations, according to the report.
OpenAI’s net loss ballooned from $5 billion in 2024 to a staggering $39 billion last year, as it continued to spend heavily on AI model development and securing compute capacity, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday, citing audited financial figures confirmed by its sources.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: OpenAI Financials Leaked Ahead Of IPO? ChatGPT Maker Said To Have Lost $39B Last Year: Here's How That Compares To Anthropic, SpaceX
OpenAI spent $34 billion on various expenses last year, according to a Financial Times report.
OpenAI’s net loss widened from $5 billion in 2024 to about $39 billion in 2025, the Financial Times reported.
Excluding restructuring charges and other non-cash items, the company’s loss was $8 billion.

OpenAI’s net loss ballooned from $5 billion in 2024 to a staggering $39 billion last year, as it continued to spend heavily on AI model development and securing compute capacity, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday, citing audited financial figures confirmed by its sources.
The ChatGPT maker spent $34 billion last year, including $19 billion on research and development and nearly $6 billion on sales, marketing, and other expenses, according to the report .
OpenAI said in March it was clocking $2 billion in monthly revenue, and Anthropic said last month that it had achieved an annual revenue run rate of $47 billion.
Anthropic’s expenditure and losses are unknown, but the Claude developer said it would report an operating profit of $559 million in the June quarter.
In March, OpenAI raised $122 billion in a funding round at a valuation of $730 billion, excluding the new investment.
Its post-money valuation came out to be $852 billion, trailing Anthropic’s $965 billion valuation.
Last week, Elon Musk’s SpaceX (which includes Musk’s AI business, xAI) listed its shares on Nasdaq in a record-shattering IPO that raised $75 billion.
SpaceX's revenue jumped 33% to $18.67 billion in 2025, but the company swung to a net loss of $4.94 billion from a profit of $791 million, according to its IPO prospectus.
Goldman has estimated ​that ⁠SpaceX's revenue would exceed $470 billion in 2030, while Morgan Stanley projected it would reach nearly $330 ⁠billion.
Reuters and other outlets previously reported that the AI giant could target a valuation of up to $1 trillion in a stock market debut as early as September.
As OpenAI’s value rose, the increased value of those investor rights resulted in a roughly $30 billion charge, according to the FT source.
According to Nasdaq Private Market, OpenAI’s valuation was last at $833.7 billion.

records.title: Moonshot Nears $30 Billion Valuation After Kimi K3 Release
records.titleEn: Moonshot Nears $30 Billion Valuation After Kimi K3 Release
records.evidence:
Moonshot's valuation had already increased from $4.3 billion in December to $20 billion within five months, supported by investors including IDG Capital, Alibaba, Meituan, a Chinese food-delivery and local-services company, and several major Chinese state funds.
For investors, Moonshot's recovery could strengthen interest in China's open-source AI sector, while its rapid valuation growth and rising revenue expectations may intensify comparisons with DeepSeek and other Chinese developers competing with OpenAI and Anthropic.
Following the Kimi K3 release, Moonshot's daily sales rose by at least six times, forcing the company to temporarily stop accepting new subscriptions because of limited computing capacity.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Moonshot Nears $30 Billion Valuation After Kimi K3 Release

/ Moonshot Nears $30 Billion Valuation After Kimi K3 Release Moonshot, a Chinese artificial intelligence startup behind the Kimi chatbot, has returned to the center of the global AI race after releasing Kimi K3, a 2.8 trillion-parameter model that attracted intense attention at the World AI Conference.
The startup is finalizing a funding round that would value it at more than $30 billion and is considering a Hong Kong public listing in as soon as six months.

Moonshot's valuation had already increased from $4.3 billion in December to $20 billion within five months, supported by investors including IDG Capital, Alibaba, Meituan, a Chinese food-delivery and local-services company, and several major Chinese state funds.
These products helped lift annual recurring revenue above $100 million in March 2026, $200 million in April and $300 million in June, according to people familiar with the figures.

Following the Kimi K3 release, Moonshot's daily sales rose by at least six times, forcing the company to temporarily stop accepting new subscriptions because of limited computing capacity.

records.title: AI is deployed in 57% of enterprises, but only 11% have hit their top two goals
records.titleEn: AI is deployed in 57% of enterprises, but only 11% have hit their top two goals
records.evidence:
The deployment of AI technology in enterprises has reached 57%, yet only 11% have achieved their primary objectives according to Kyndryl's 2026 People Readiness Report.
While 61% have redesigned roles to support AI adoption and 24% are creating new AI-focused management positions, only one-third have fully implemented employee training programs focused on working alongside AI tools.
Fifty-seven percent of enterprises now have AI embedded in core business processes or deployed broadly across their organizations, up from 35% just one year ago.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: The deployment of AI technology in enterprises has reached 57%, yet only 11% have achieved their primary objectives according to Kyndryl's 2026 People Readiness Report.
Fifty-seven percent of enterprises now have AI embedded in core business processes or deployed broadly across their organizations, up from 35% just one year ago.
Worldwide AI spending is forecast to reach $2.52 trillion in 2026, a 44% year-over-year increase, according to Gartner research cited in Kyndryl's report.

The Achievers Workforce Institute 's seventh annual State of Recognition Report, cited by MarketScale, found that just 19% of workers feel confident using AI tools, and only 18% feel supported in adapting to them.
Kyndryl's report isolates a cohort it calls Pacesetters: roughly 9% of respondents that are generating measurable AI returns.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: IT Services Market Size To Exceed $3.35 Trillion By 2035

The global IT Services Market is entering a new phase of expansion as organizations across industries modernize technology ecosystems to improve operational efficiency, strengthen cyber resilience, and accelerate digital innovation. “According to a recent study by SNS Insider, the IT Services Market size valued at USD 1.50 trillion in 2025, is anticipated to grow to USD 3.35 trillion by 2035, registering a CAGR of 8.35% over the 2026–2035 forecast period.” With more companies turning towards the cloud, enterprise software, artificial intelligence, and connected infrastructure, the demand for managed and professional IT services is growing.

Key Market Insights Highlight Changing Enterprise Technology Priorities Based on type, Operations & Maintenance accounted for approximately 54.1% of market revenue in 2025 due to the continuous need for infrastructure support, application maintenance, and performance optimization.
By approach, Proactive IT Services represented around 58.5% of total revenue in 2025 owing to growing adoption of preventive monitoring and predictive maintenance strategies.
In terms of application, Systems & Network Management held nearly 47.8% market share in 2025 as businesses prioritize uninterrupted IT operations across hybrid infrastructure environments.

North America Held 36.5% of the IT Services Market Share in 2025; Asia Pacific Projected to Register the Fastest CAGR Through 2035 In 2025, the North American market is projected to account for around 36.5% of the global market revenue, largely due to high enterprise technology spending and cloud adoption, managed services, and cybersecurity investments across sectors.
